decisions.title: AuthService as a module separate from UserService
decisions.rationale: Login (AC1-3), the AC4 startup migration, and the AC5 provisioning script all need UserRepository access for password_hash/must_reset_password, and UserService already owns CRUD business rules for the same User model. A new AuthService keeps auth and CRUD concerns independently testable and reviewable per the reusability baseline's single-responsibility rule, and lets AUTH-02-TC-11 assert the module boundary mechanically.

decisions.title: In-process sliding-window counter for login rate-limiting (v1)
decisions.rationale: The security baseline requires auth endpoints throttled per hashed email at 3/60min rolling with HTTP 429, but no shared cache exists in this stack and the deployment target is single-server, so a new external dependency solely for rate-limiting is not justified. An in-process dict keyed by hashed email with pruned attempt timestamps satisfies the requirement without new infrastructure.

decisions.title: AC5 password input via interactive getpass stdin prompt, never a CLI argument
decisions.rationale: The AC5 operator script must accept a real plaintext password without ever persisting it to shell history or exposing it via ps/process listing. Python's stdlib getpass.getpass() provides a non-echoing stdin prompt at zero additional dependency cost, eliminating both exposure vectors that a CLI argument would introduce.

decisions.title: password_hash and must_reset_password columns land now, in AUTH-02, ahead of AUTH-03
decisions.rationale: AUTH-02's own AC4/AC5 test cases require seeding fixture rows with and without a password_hash value and asserting real column state after migration/script runs, which is impossible without the column existing in the schema today. AUTH-02 is required to be independently testable now, not gated on AUTH-03 landing first, so the columns are added here with a stdlib-only placeholder hash (hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac) that AUTH-03 will later replace with the real argon2id/bcrypt scheme against the same columns.

decisions.title: Real JWT signing via PyJWT (HS256, JWT_SECRET_KEY) replaces the stub token
decisions.rationale: A cross-plan audit during AUTH-08's planning found that no story across the AUTH epic actually implements JWT signing/verification: AUTH-02's AuthService.login returned a stub LoginResponse{token: str} with no JWT library and no use of JWT_SECRET_KEY (AUTH-08's accepted risk R-08-jwt-signing-not-yet-implemented); AUTH-03 only hashes passwords; AUTH-04 is frontend-only and only decodes the exp claim client-side. Since AuthService.login is the only place a token is issued, and JWT_SECRET_KEY is already documented and startup-validated by AUTH-08, this story is the correct owner to close the gap. PyJWT (minimal, no unnecessary crypto-backend complexity vs python-jose) with HS256 (symmetric, appropriate for a single-backend-service internal admin tool with no separate issuing/verifying services) signs a two-claim payload (sub: user email, exp: now+60min per AUTH-04's locked TTL) so AUTH-04's existing jwt-decode exp-only check keeps working unmodified.
